scene: Kyoto Ninenzaka / Sannenzaka — closed spherical adaptation
authorization: User requests a new spherical closed-loop scene, explicitly preserving the existing scene. Existing session authorizes native Blender assets, Three.js runtime and publication.
preserved: All previously tracked source files, including kyoto.html, index.html and sannen-*
topology: Eight existing street segments: western Sannenzaka connects artistically to the eastern Kiyomizuzaka endpoint. Ninenzaka and the short western Kiyomizuzaka segment remain branches. This is not a real geographic connection.
source: ../sannenzaka/source.osm.xml.gz, OSM attribution retained in the new page
buildings: 121 of 142 original mapped anchors retained, positioned along the folded street sequence; remaining anchors omitted when they cannot be placed with street/house clearance. No additional building locations invented as geographic facts.
surface: Periodic, asymmetric spherical ribbon. Existing terrain footprint has backing and a plain irregular earth support; this underside is not mapped or walkable. No extra streets or polar vegetation rings.
collision: Existing metric walk surface and door openings in unfolded coordinates; short swept steps wrap the seam. Native opaque curved geometry constrains camera rays.
player: Independent native Resident, WASD/arrows and touch joystick, nearby left-click/E and touch button, local radial camera up, phase and heading continuous through seam
nativeAssets: Read-only reuse of original Blender GLBs. New spatial assembly and periodic navigation are implemented in Three.js. Current assembled geometry exported to Blender for offline review.
camera: Whole small world default; panoramic drag/zoom, landmark views, NPC follow and player exploration. Portrait overview uses aspect-based fit.
limitations: Artistic reordering and bending of a real-map-derived scene, not geodetically accurate
